target_stack.rationale: PB-005: team's existing expertise, not a technical derivation

evidence.notes: runtime_ingestion: ticketd/ops/access.log supplied and parsed (P2), but it is a single synthetic day (12/Jul/2026) replayed on repeating 61-entry timestamp cycles, one user identity (jdoe@corp.example.com), one user-agent (svc-ui/2.1), and randomized source IPs -- NOT the genuine ~30-day window described in the rewrite request. Endpoint frequency ratios and the 5xx/429 status counts are usable evidence (PB-004); anything requiring real temporal spread, per-user behavior, or a true zero-traffic guarantee (do-not-port calls) is capped at reduced confidence -- see OQ-003. P9 AUDIT FINDING (2026-08-09, independently verified by the generator): the log's per-endpoint SUCCESS status codes do not all match the pinned commit's actual behavior -- of 423 POST /api/tickets requests, 411 show status 200 and ZERO show 201, but create_ticket() unconditionally returns 201 on success (ticketd/app/server.py:55, confirmed by every P7 trace). This means the access log was NOT literally generated by running this exact pinned commit end-to-end -- it is synthetic/placeholder traffic-SHAPE data, not a genuine capture. The frequency ratios and error-rate percentages still check out arithmetically (independently re-verified) and remain usable for relative usage-weighting, but do not treat this log as ground truth for anything status-code-specific, and do not describe it elsewhere in this workspace as more authentic than it is. data_census: inactive, no production SQLite file or Postgres dump was supplied, only db/schema.sql (DDL). census.py was still run against the DDL to pre-stage docs/migration/census-queries.sql for when real data is available. trace_capture_t1: still inactive (no production request/response capture exists), BUT P7 upgraded the replay corpus beyond static T3: the legacy app was actually booted locally (verification/harness/run-legacy.sh, validated) and 22 real HTTP traces were captured across verification/replay/traces/*.jsonl -- genuine T2 (scripted sessions against real legacy execution), not T3 (statically derived). This directly resolved OQ-008 (an inferred-only claim, now traced) and surfaced a new, previously-unknown root cause for PB-004 (a SQLite connection-leak causing intermittent 'database is locked' 500s -- see docs/problem-brief.md PB-004 and verification/README.md). The harness baseline (legacy traces vs themselves, no divergences) passes 100% (13/13, 3/3, 6/6) and 35/35 L2 characterization tests pass. Known gap: drive_trace.py (the L3 live-modern driver) cannot yet observe the side_effects block (notification dispatch, token mechanism) over HTTP alone -- ED-001/ED-001b/ED-002 need modern/ to expose an equivalent hook before L3 meaningfully verifies PB-001/PB-002's REPAIR dispositions; see verification/README.md.
